newsitem.title: USA: Blacks guilty in Hasidic Jew's killing in New York.
newsitem.headline: Blacks guilty in Hasidic Jew's killing in New York.

text.p: A federal jury on Monday found two black men guilty in the fatal stabbing of a Hasidic Jew in a case stemming from 1991 racial violence in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn.
No sentencing date was set.
At issue was whether the defendants were part of a mob that killed Australian Yankel Rosenbaum or were scapegoats for the Jewish student's murder during four nights of rioting.
Lemrick Nelson, 21, who was acquitted earlier of the murder in state court, was convicted after four days of deliberations of violating Rosenbaum's civil rights.
Hasidic Jews and elected officials demanded a federal investigation after the acquittal by the state court jury. That inquiry led to this trial.
A co-defendant, 43-year-old Charles Price, was convicted of aiding and abetting the civil rights violation by inciting the crowd to seek revenge on Jews.
Nelson buried his head in his hands and cried when he heard the guilty verdict.
Both men face the possiblity of life in prison, although such sentences are unlikely due to circumstances and legal technicalities in the case.
Rosenbaum's brother, Norman, a tax attorney from Melbourne, Australia, who fought for the federal trial, said: "This is one small step for justice and one giant leap for the justice system."

However, he added, "There's still the rest of the mob out there, still on the street, equally responsible for my brother's murder. Each and every person responsible for my brother's murder will be brought to justice."
However, U.S. Attorney Zachary Carter said there would be no further criminal prosecutions in the case because the statute of limitations had run out.

Still pending are civil lawsuits, including one filed by Jewish community members in Crown Heights against the city and police and one filed by the Rosenbaum family against Kings County Hospital, which treated the dying man.

The Rosenbaum murder was sparked by a car accident in which a Hasidic driver hit and killed a 7-year-old black child. The incident occurred in Crown Heights, a frequent site of friction between blacks and Hasidic Jews.
The jury, which included two Jews and three blacks, came back with its verdict after watching a videotape of the scene made by a bystander.
The Crown Heights neighbourhood was calm in the wake of the verdict, and police said there were no signs of unrest.
"We expect and anticipate that everyone will accept this verdict peacefully," said Mayor Rudolph Giuliani. "If you expect and anticipate that kind of behaviour, you get it."
He called the case "a very sad chapter in the history of our city."

Defence lawyers argued Nelson and Price did not commit the crimes. "Lemrick Nelson was made the sacrificial lamb. The police framed him, set him up," said his lawyer Christine Yaris, during closing arguments.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Valerie Caproni said strong testimony came from Nelson's ex-girlfriend Travionne Shaw.
"Lemrick Nelson told her a story that only one other person in the world knew, and Yankel Rosenbaum took it to his grave," Caproni said.
